question: Which among the following is India's first Human spaceflight programme?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gaganyaan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gaganyaan" is India's first human spaceflight programme, undertaken by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). It aims to send a crew of Indian astronauts ("Vyomanauts"/Gaganyatris) into Low Earth Orbit (about 400 km) aboard an indigenous crew module. (गगनयान — भारत का पहला मानव अंतरिक्ष उड़ान कार्यक्रम)

• The mission was announced by the Prime Minister on 15 August 2018 and uses the human-rated LVM3 (GSLV Mk-III) launch vehicle from Sriharikota.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Shukrayaan — ISRO's proposed mission to Venus.

• Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission, 2013) — India's first interplanetary mission; India became the first country to reach Mars in its maiden attempt.

• Chandrayaan-1 (2008) — India's first lunar mission, which confirmed the presence of water molecules on the Moon.

NOTE

• ISRO was founded in 1969; its headquarters are at Bengaluru and it works under the Department of Space.

• Rakesh Sharma became the first Indian in space in 1984, aboard the Soviet Soyuz T-11.

question: When did Mahatma Gandhi founded the All India Harijan Sevak Sangh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1932.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mahatma Gandhi founded the All India Harijan Sevak Sangh (originally the "All India Anti-Untouchability League") in 1932, to work for the eradication of untouchability and the upliftment of the depressed classes, whom he called "Harijans" (children of God). (हरिजन सेवक संघ — 1932)

• Its first president was Ghanshyam Das Birla and its first secretary was Amritlal Thakkar (Thakkar Bapa).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Sangh was set up soon after the Poona Pact (24 September 1932) between Gandhi and Dr B. R. Ambedkar, which replaced separate electorates for the depressed classes with reserved seats in the general electorate.

• Gandhi began his Harijan weekly newspaper in 1933 and undertook a nationwide Harijan Yatra.

NOTE

• Untouchability was abolished by Article 17 of the Indian Constitution; the practice is punishable under the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955.

question: 'Galpaguchchha', written by Rabindranath Tagore is a collection of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is short stories.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Galpaguchchha" (literally "a bunch of stories") is a celebrated collection of short stories in Bengali written by Rabindranath Tagore. It contains about 84 stories, including famous ones such as "Kabuliwala", "The Postmaster" and "Hungry Stones". (गल्पगुच्छ — लघु कथाओं का संग्रह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Rabindranath Tagore (1861–1941) was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for Gitanjali, becoming the first non-European and the first Indian to win a Nobel Prize.

• He wrote India's national anthem "Jana Gana Mana" and Bangladesh's "Amar Shonar Bangla"; Sri Lanka's national anthem was also inspired by him.

• He renounced his knighthood in 1919 in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

NOTE

• Other works of Tagore: Gora, Ghare Baire (The Home and the World), Chokher Bali, Sadhana, Post Office, Gitanjali.

question: Who among the following won the most number of Grand Slam Tournaments in Men's Tennis Singles as of 25th October 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rafael Nadal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of 25 October 2022, Rafael Nadal of Spain held the record for the most Men's Singles Grand Slam titles — 22, ahead of Novak Djokovic (21) and Roger Federer (20). Nadal had won the Australian Open and the French Open in 2022. (राफेल नडाल — 22 ग्रैंड स्लैम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Nadal is nicknamed the "King of Clay" for his record 14 French Open (Roland Garros) titles.

• Pete Sampras (USA) won 14 Grand Slam singles titles.

• The four Grand Slams are the Australian Open (hard), French Open (clay), Wimbledon (grass) and the US Open (hard).

NOTE

• Wimbledon, started in 1877, is the oldest tennis tournament in the world.

• India's Grand Slam winners in doubles/mixed doubles include Leander Paes, Mahesh Bhupathi, Sania Mirza and Rohan Bopanna.

question: ______ is the heaviest naturally occuring element of Periodic Table with an atomic weight of 238.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uranium.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Uranium (U)" is the heaviest naturally occurring element in the periodic table, with atomic number 92 and an atomic mass of about 238 u (the most abundant isotope being U-238). (यूरेनियम — परमाणु क्रमांक 92)

• It is a radioactive metal, discovered by Martin Heinrich Klaproth (1789) and named after the planet Uranus.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• U-235 is the fissile isotope used as fuel in nuclear reactors and atom bombs; natural uranium contains only about 0.7% U-235.

• Xenon (Xe, 54) is a noble gas used in lamps; Helium (He, 2) is the second-lightest element; Mercury (Hg, 80) is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature.

NOTE

• India's major uranium mine is at Jaduguda (Jharkhand); thorium reserves are large in the monazite sands of Kerala, central to India's three-stage nuclear programme designed by Dr Homi J. Bhabha.

question: The feature of Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the ______ Constitution
solution_text:
The correct answer is Irish.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), contained in Part IV (Articles 36–51) of the Indian Constitution, were borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland (Irish Constitution), which had itself taken the idea from the Spanish Constitution. (नीति निदेशक तत्व — आयरलैंड से)

• DPSPs are non-justiciable (not enforceable in a court) but are "fundamental in the governance of the country" (Article 37).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other borrowed features:

◦ British — parliamentary system, rule of law, single citizenship, cabinet system, writs.

◦ US — Fundamental Rights, independent judiciary, judicial review, impeachment of the President.

◦ Irish — DPSP, nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha, method of election of the President.

◦ Canadian — federation with a strong Centre, residuary powers with the Centre, appointment of Governors.

◦ USSR (erstwhile) — Fundamental Duties, ideals of justice in the Preamble.

NOTE

• The Government of India Act, 1935 is the single largest source of the Constitution (federal scheme, office of Governor, emergency provisions, public service commissions).

question: __________ is a festival of sowing seeds in the field. It is a major festival celebrated in Jharkhand.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rohini.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rohini" is a festival of sowing seeds in the fields, celebrated in Jharkhand. It is regarded as one of the earliest festivals of the agricultural year, when farmers ceremonially begin sowing paddy seeds. (रोहिणी — बीज बोने का पर्व, झारखंड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other festivals of Jharkhand:

◦ Karam — celebrated in honour of the Karam tree (Karam Devta), the deity of youth and fertility, with dancing around a Karam branch.

◦ Sarhul — the spring festival marking the worship of the Sal tree and Mother Nature; the New Year of the tribal community.

◦ Bandana (Sohrai) — a cattle festival celebrated during Kartik Amavasya.

◦ Tusu Parab — a harvest festival celebrated in the month of Poush.

NOTE

• Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar on 15 November 2000 (birth anniversary of Birsa Munda); its capital is Ranchi.

question: In which year was the 5G telecommunications technology launched in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2022.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 5G telecommunications services were formally launched in India by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 1 October 2022 at the India Mobile Congress in New Delhi. (भारत में 5G — 2022)

• The 5G spectrum auction was held in July–August 2022, and services were rolled out initially in major cities by Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• 5G (fifth-generation mobile network) offers ultra-high speed (up to 10 Gbps), very low latency and support for a massive number of connected devices (IoT).

• Generations: 1G (analogue voice), 2G (digital voice + SMS), 3G (mobile internet), 4G/LTE (high-speed broadband), 5G (ultra-broadband, IoT, machine-to-machine).

NOTE

• The telecom regulator in India is TRAI (Telecom Regulatory Authority of India, 1997), and the nodal ministry is the Ministry of Communications (Department of Telecommunications).

question: Which among the following book was NOT written by King Harshavardhana?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amuktamalayada.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Amuktamalyada" was NOT written by Harshavardhana — it is a Telugu work composed by Krishnadevaraya, the greatest ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire (Tuluva dynasty, r. 1509–1529). (अमुक्तमाल्यदा — कृष्णदेवराय)

• Harshavardhana (r. 606–647 CE), of the Pushyabhuti (Vardhana) dynasty of Thanesar/Kannauj, wrote three Sanskrit plays: Ratnavali, Nagananda and Priyadarshika.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Harsha's court poet was Banabhatta, author of Harshacharita (a biography of Harsha) and Kadambari.

• The Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) visited India during Harsha's reign and described it in Si-yu-ki.

• Harsha was defeated on the banks of the Narmada by the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II.

NOTE

• Krishnadevaraya was praised as "Andhra Bhoja"; the Portuguese travellers Domingo Paes and Duarte Barbosa visited his court at Hampi (Vijayanagara).

question: According to Census 2011, which among the following is the least populous Union territory in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lakshadweep.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of 2011, Lakshadweep was the least populous Union Territory (and the least populous unit) of India, with a population of about 64,473. (लक्षद्वीप — सबसे कम जनसंख्या वाला केंद्र शासित प्रदेश)

• Lakshadweep is also the smallest Union Territory by area (32 sq km); its capital is Kavaratti.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Census 2011 highlights:

◦ Most populous state — Uttar Pradesh; least populous state — Sikkim.

◦ Most populous UT — Delhi; least populous UT — Lakshadweep.

◦ Highest literacy — Kerala; lowest literacy — Bihar.

◦ Highest sex ratio — Kerala (1084); lowest — Haryana (879).

NOTE

• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years; the first synchronous census was in 1881 under Lord Ripon, while the census was begun in 1872 under Lord Mayo.

question: Who among the following was the founder of the Khilji Dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jalal-ud-din Firoz Khilji.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jalal-ud-din Firoz Khilji founded the Khilji (Khalji) dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate in 1290 CE, after overthrowing the last ruler of the Slave (Mamluk) dynasty. He ruled until 1296, when he was murdered by his nephew and son-in-law Alauddin Khilji. (जलालुद्दीन फ़िरोज़ ख़िलजी — ख़िलजी वंश के संस्थापक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Alauddin Khilji (1296–1316) was the most powerful Khilji ruler — known for his market/price control regulations, a permanent standing army, the Deccan campaigns led by Malik Kafur, and the building of the Alai Darwaza and Siri Fort.

• Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah was the last effective Khilji ruler; Nasiruddin Khusrau Shah briefly usurped the throne in 1320 before Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq founded the Tughlaq dynasty.

NOTE

• Dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate (1206–1526): Slave/Mamluk (1206), Khilji (1290), Tughlaq (1320), Sayyid (1414), Lodi (1451).

question: Which law of economics state "Bad money drives out good money"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gresham's Law.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gresham's Law" states that "bad money drives out good money" — when two kinds of money of the same legal value are in circulation, people hoard the "good" (intrinsically more valuable) money and spend the "bad" (debased) money, so the good money disappears from circulation. (ग्रेशम का नियम)

• It is named after Sir Thomas Gresham, a financial agent of Queen Elizabeth I of England.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The law works only when both currencies are legal tender at a fixed exchange rate.

• Ohm's Law (V = IR) belongs to physics; Gauss's Law relates electric flux to enclosed charge; "Baxter's Law" is not a recognised economic law.

NOTE

• Related economics laws for SSC: Law of Demand, Law of Supply, Say's Law of Markets ("supply creates its own demand"), Engel's Law (share of income spent on food falls as income rises), Giffen's paradox.

question: Governor general Lord Dalhousie described the Kingdom of ______ "as a cherry that will drop into our mouth one day".
solution_text:
The correct answer is Awadh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lord Dalhousie (Governor-General, 1848–1856) described the kingdom of Awadh (Oudh) as "a cherry that will drop into our mouth one day". He annexed Awadh in 1856 on the pretext of misgovernment, deposing Nawab Wajid Ali Shah. (अवध — डलहौज़ी की "चेरी" टिप्पणी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Dalhousie is best known for the Doctrine of Lapse, under which he annexed Satara (1848), Jaitpur and Sambalpur (1849), Udaipur (1852), Jhansi (1853) and Nagpur (1854).

• Other reforms of Dalhousie: the first railway line (Bombay–Thane, 1853), the telegraph (Calcutta–Agra), the Post Office Act 1854, Wood's Despatch (1854) on education, and the Public Works Department.

NOTE

• The annexation of Awadh caused deep resentment among the sepoys of the Bengal Army, many of whom came from Awadh, and was an important cause of the Revolt of 1857.

question: Which among the following dances is also known as Ekaharya, where one dancer takes on many roles in a single performance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatnatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bharatanatyam is also known as "Ekaharya", because in it a single dancer takes on many roles/characters in a single performance ("eka" = one, "harya" = one who carries/portrays). (एकहार्य — भरतनाट्यम)

• It is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra of Bharata Muni, and was traditionally performed in temples by devadasis.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Its repertoire follows a sequence: Alarippu, Jatiswaram, Shabdam, Varnam, Padam, Tillana.

• Famous exponents: Rukmini Devi Arundale, Balasaraswati, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Padma Subrahmanyam, Mallika Sarabhai.

• Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Kathakali (Kerala) and Kathak (North India) are other classical forms; Kathakali is largely a group/dance-drama form with elaborate make-up.

NOTE

• The eight classical dance forms recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

question: The Blackbuck National Park is located in _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Blackbuck National Park is located at Velavadar in the Bhavnagar district of Gujarat. Established in 1976, it is famous for the blackbuck (Antilope cervicapra), and also for the wolf, lesser florican and large harrier roosts. (काला हिरण राष्ट्रीय उद्यान — वेलावदर, गुजरात)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The blackbuck is the state animal of Punjab, Haryana and Andhra Pradesh, and is protected under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

• Other national parks of Gujarat: Gir National Park (Asiatic lion), Marine National Park, Gulf of Kachchh (India's first marine national park), Vansda National Park.

NOTE

• India's first national park was Hailey National Park (1936), now Jim Corbett National Park in Uttarakhand.

• Project Tiger was launched in 1973 and Project Elephant in 1992.

question: Which among the following is not an example of Thallophyta?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Marchantia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Marchantia" is not a thallophyte — it is a liverwort, belonging to the division Bryophyta (often called the "amphibians of the plant kingdom"). (मार्केंशिया — ब्रायोफाइटा)

• Thallophyta are the simplest plants, having an undifferentiated thallus (no true root, stem or leaf); the group includes algae (and, in the older classification, fungi).

• Spirogyra, Chara and Cladophora are all green algae (Chlorophyceae), i.e., thallophytes.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Classification of the plant kingdom (Whittaker/Eichler scheme used in NCERT): Thallophyta → Bryophyta → Pteridophyta → Gymnosperms → Angiosperms.

• Bryophytes have a simple body with rhizoids, need water for reproduction, and lack vascular tissue; Pteridophytes (ferns) are the first plants with xylem and phloem.

NOTE

• Examples: Thallophyta — Spirogyra, Ulothrix, Chara, Cladophora; Bryophyta — Marchantia, Riccia, Funaria, Moss; Pteridophyta — Fern, Marsilea, Equisetum.

question: Bhimsen Joshi was one of the greatest Indian vocalists from _______, in the Hindustani classical tradition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Bhimsen Joshi (1922–2011) was born at Gadag in Karnataka and was one of the greatest Hindustani classical vocalists of India. He belonged to the Kirana Gharana and was a disciple of Sawai Gandharva. (भीमसेन जोशी — कर्नाटक)

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2008 — the highest civilian award of India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• He is remembered for his khayal renditions and for the popular national-integration song "Mile Sur Mera Tumhara".

• He also received the Padma Shri (1972), Padma Bhushan (1985), Padma Vibhushan (1999) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

NOTE

• Hindustani gharanas: Kirana, Gwalior, Agra, Jaipur-Atrauli, Patiala, Rampur-Sahaswan.

• Other Bharat Ratna musicians: M. S. Subbulakshmi (1998), Ravi Shankar (1999), Lata Mangeshkar (2001), Ustad Bismillah Khan (2001).

question: The High court of Delhi was established in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1966.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The High Court of Delhi was established on 31 October 1966 under the Delhi High Court Act, 1966. Before this, Delhi came under the jurisdiction of the Punjab High Court. (दिल्ली उच्च न्यायालय — 1966)

• Its seat is at New Delhi, and its jurisdiction extends over the National Capital Territory of Delhi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Article 214 provides that there shall be a High Court for each State; Article 231 allows a common High Court for two or more States/UTs.

• The oldest High Courts in India are those of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras, all established in 1862; the Allahabad High Court was set up in 1866.

• Judges of a High Court are appointed by the President and hold office until the age of 62 years.

NOTE

• As of recent years, India has 25 High Courts. The Supreme Court of India was inaugurated on 28 January 1950.

question: The Department of Pharmaceuticals has given 'in-principle' approval to the proposals to set up bulk drug parks in three states- Himachal Pradesh, Gujarat and _______ under the scheme of "Promotion of Bulk Drug Parks".
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the scheme "Promotion of Bulk Drug Parks", the Department of Pharmaceuticals granted 'in-principle' approval to three states — Himachal Pradesh, Gujarat and Andhra Pradesh — for setting up bulk drug parks. (आंध्र प्रदेश)

• The scheme provides financial assistance of up to Rs 1,000 crore or 70% of the project cost of common infrastructure facilities per park, to reduce India's import dependence on bulk drugs/APIs (Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients), chiefly from China.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The scheme, approved in 2020 with an outlay of about Rs 3,000 crore, comes under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers.

• A complementary Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for bulk drugs and medical devices was launched at the same time.

NOTE

• India is called the "Pharmacy of the World" — it is the largest supplier of generic medicines globally and a leading vaccine producer.

question: Which famous Indian Kathak dancer received the Padma Vibhushan, India's second highest civilian award, in 1986?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Birju Maharaj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Birju Maharaj (1938–2022), the doyen of the Kathak dance form and the leading exponent of the Lucknow "Kalka-Bindadin" Gharana, received the Padma Vibhushan — India's second highest civilian award — in 1986. (बिरजू महाराज — पद्म विभूषण, 1986)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• He also won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and the Kalidas Samman, and choreographed for films such as Devdas, Bajirao Mastani and Dedh Ishqiya (National Film Award for Best Choreography, 2012).

• Manjari Chaturvedi is known for Sufi Kathak, Madhavi Mudgal for Odissi, and Mallika Sarabhai for Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi.

NOTE

• Order of civilian awards: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri. They were instituted in 1954.

• Kathak is the only major classical dance form of North India with strong Persian/Mughal court influences; other gharanas are Jaipur, Banaras and Raigarh.

question: The ancient name of which of the following rivers is Vipasha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Beas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Vipasha" is the ancient (Vedic) name of the river Beas. It rises near the Rohtang Pass in Himachal Pradesh (Beas Kund) and joins the Sutlej near Harike in Punjab. (व्यास नदी — विपाशा)

• Alexander's eastward march is said to have stopped at the Beas (called Hyphasis by the Greeks).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Vedic/ancient names of the Punjab rivers:

◦ Sutlej — Shutudri (Zaradros)

◦ Ravi — Parushni/Iravati (Hydraotes)

◦ Chenab — Asikni/Chandrabhaga (Acesines)

◦ Jhelum — Vitasta (Hydaspes)

◦ Beas — Vipasha (Hyphasis)

◦ Indus — Sindhu

NOTE

• Under the Indus Waters Treaty (1960), India has full rights over the eastern rivers — Ravi, Beas and Sutlej, while Pakistan gets the western rivers — Indus, Jhelum and Chenab.

question: According to 2011 Census, which among the following states has the highest literacy rate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of 2011, Kerala had the highest literacy rate among Indian states — about 94% (93.91%). (केरल — सर्वाधिक साक्षरता दर)

• India's overall literacy rate in 2011 was 74.04% (male 82.14%, female 65.46%).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Lakshadweep (91.85%) and Mizoram (91.33%) followed Kerala; Bihar (61.8%) had the lowest literacy rate.

• Literacy is defined as the ability of a person aged 7 years and above to read and write with understanding in any language.

NOTE

• The 2011 Census was the 15th national census and the 7th since Independence; its theme/slogan was "Our Census, Our Future".

• Kerala also leads in sex ratio (1084 females per 1000 males) and in most human-development indicators.

question: Which of the following cities was the first planned city of the Mughals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fatehpur Sikri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Fatehpur Sikri, built by Emperor Akbar from 1571, was the first planned city of the Mughals and served as the Mughal capital for about 15 years before being abandoned (largely due to water scarcity). (फ़तेहपुर सीकरी — मुगलों का पहला नियोजित नगर)

• Akbar founded it to honour the Sufi saint Sheikh Salim Chishti, and named it "Fatehpur" (City of Victory) after his conquest of Gujarat.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Important structures at Fatehpur Sikri: Buland Darwaza (the highest gateway in India, built in 1576 to commemorate the Gujarat victory), Jama Masjid, Panch Mahal, Diwan-i-Khas, Ibadat Khana (where Akbar held religious discussions) and the tomb of Salim Chishti.

• Fatehpur Sikri is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1986), located in the Agra district of Uttar Pradesh.

NOTE

• Akbar's religious policy: abolition of jizya (1564) and pilgrim tax, the Din-i-Ilahi (1582) and the policy of Sulh-i-kul (peace with all).

question: Lok Sabha has a fixed term of _______ years and can be dissolved by the President at any time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Lok Sabha (House of the People) has a normal term of five years from the date of its first sitting, but it can be dissolved earlier by the President at any time on the advice of the Council of Ministers. (लोकसभा का कार्यकाल — 5 वर्ष)

• During a National Emergency, its term can be extended by Parliament for one year at a time, but not beyond six months after the emergency ceases.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house and is never dissolved; one-third of its members retire every two years, each member having a term of six years.

• Maximum strength of the Lok Sabha: 552 (530 from states + 20 from UTs + earlier 2 nominated Anglo-Indians, discontinued by the 104th Amendment, 2019).

• Minimum age to be a member: 25 years for the Lok Sabha and 30 years for the Rajya Sabha.

NOTE

• The Speaker presides over the Lok Sabha; the Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. Money Bills can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha (Article 110).

question: The International Cricket Council (ICC) Women's Cricket World Cup 2022 was hosted by ________ in March and April 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Zealand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The ICC Women's Cricket World Cup 2022 was hosted by New Zealand in March–April 2022. (न्यूज़ीलैंड)

• Australia won the title — their seventh Women's World Cup — by defeating England by 71 runs in the final at Christchurch on 3 April 2022. Alyssa Healy scored 170 in the final and was named Player of the Tournament.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• It was the 12th edition of the tournament; the event was postponed from 2021 to 2022 because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

• The first Women's Cricket World Cup was held in England in 1973 — two years before the first men's World Cup (1975).

• India reached the final in 2005 and 2017, finishing runners-up on both occasions.

NOTE

• The ICC was founded in 1909 (as the Imperial Cricket Conference) and has its headquarters in Dubai, UAE.
